slides.title: High Fidelity Capture, Reconstruction, and Transfer of Human Demonstrations for Robot-Assisted Bathing
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for capturing and transferring contact-rich human bathing demonstrations to robots, contributing to the development of safe physical human-robot interaction (pHRI) relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: A framework for capturing and transferring high-fidelity human bathing demonstrations to a robot-assisted system.
card.key_idea: Uses contact regions as processing primitives to reconstruct synchronized motion, shape, and force, enabling retargeting to a tendon-driven soft hand and robotic arm.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using a dataset of 128 captures (3 clinicians, 6 subjects) and real-world deployment on a mannequin via open- and closed-loop control.
card.limitation: Substantial sim-to-real gap; closed-loop control uses aggregate pressure sums rather than distributions; not yet ready for human subjects.

slides.title: Detection and Ranging of Transient Extrinsic Contacts Based on 6D Dynamic Tactile Sensing
slides.tldr: FAST EXTRINSIC CONTACT DETECTION AND RANGING
slides.highlight: This work introduces TECDAR for rapid, millimeter-level localization of extrinsic contacts, supporting the physics-based skill estimation and tactile sensing goals of MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: TECDAR enables fast, millimeter-level extrinsic contact localization using a single 6D IMU and Bayesian filtering.
card.key_idea: An event-driven framework using an accelerometer to trigger contact detection and a gyroscope with an Extended Kalman Filter to map rotational transients to contact coordinates.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on line and point-contact tasks (e.g., books, pens) achieving ~7mm average accuracy and 20ms control response cycles.
card.limitation: Localization error is higher (5.36mm) compared to high-resolution visuo-tactile sensors like GelSlim 3.0.

slides.title: AdaDexGrasp: Adaptive Dexterous Grasping via 3D Visuo-Tactile Representation Fusion
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE DEXTEROUS GRASPING VIA VISUO-TACTILE FUSION
slides.highlight: This framework integrates 3D visual perception with tactile feedback to enable contact-aware grasp generation and dynamic refinement, improving success rates across diverse objects.

card.one_liner: AdaDexGrasp improves dexterous grasping by fusing 3D geometry with tactile feedback for adaptive pose refinement.
card.key_idea: A framework using a semantic contact map for initial pose generation and a tactile-mapped point cloud for iterative, closed-loop grasp stability prediction and pose adaptation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in IsaacGym and real-world (Psibot hand) across seen/unseen objects. Outperformed 10 baselines, achieving 83% success on unseen categories in simulation.
card.limitation: Denser tactile modalities (e.g., shear forces) increased data requirements and widened the sim-to-real gap, necessitating a simpler representation.

slides.title: Near-sensor Computing for Rapid Visuotactile Perception
slides.tldr: NEAR-SENSOR COMPUTING FOR RAPID VISUOTACTILE PERCEPTION
slides.highlight: A near-sensor computing framework using a streaming hardware pipeline reduces latency and power consumption for visuotactile sensing. This enables faster robotic protective reflex loops compared to host-based processing.

card.one_liner: A near-sensor computing framework enables rapid, deterministic 3D visuotactile reconstruction for ultrafast robotic protective reflexes.
card.key_idea: A streaming hardware pipeline implementing a spectral Poisson solver using discrete sine transforms, providing fixed-latency depth reconstruction without iterative convergence or host-based processing.
card.evaluation: Tested on 15 geometries (0.17% RMS error vs reference) and a robot reflex loop (28.3ms vs 169.9ms host-based). Results appear trustworthy.
card.limitation: Maximum supported grid size is currently limited by available on-chip memory for transform buffering.

slides.title: VIDP: Variable Impedance Diffusion Policy for Compliant Robot Manipulation from Diverse Demonstrations
slides.tldr: VARIABLE IMPEDANCE DIFFUSION POLICY FOR COMPLIANT MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This framework enables robots to learn variable impedance control from kinematic demonstrations without force sensors, improving success rates in contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: VIDP learns variable impedance control from kinematic demonstrations to enable compliant robot manipulation without force sensors.
card.key_idea: Uses a Task-Parameterized Directionality-Aware Mixture Model (TP-DAMM) to extract trajectory distributions from demonstrations and map them to stiffness profiles and pose actions.
card.evaluation: Real-world experiments compared VIDP against fixed-impedance baselines, measuring task success rate, interaction forces, and tracking errors.

slides.title: Trajectory Divergence Horizon Decision for Reliable Dual-Arm Surgical Subtask Manipulation
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE EXECUTION HORIZON FOR SURGICAL VLA MODELS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a test-time mechanism to improve the reliability of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models in surgical robotics by adaptively truncating action sequences based on trajectory divergence.

card.one_liner: TDHD improves surgical VLA reliability by adaptively truncating open-loop action sequences based on trajectory divergence.
card.key_idea: A test-time mechanism that measures L2 distance between two flow-matching trajectories generated with slight noise perturbations to trigger timely replanning via dual-threshold rules.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a da Vinci-like dual-arm robot using 600 teleoperated demonstrations; success rates rose to 60% (needle) and 80% (tissue) over VLA baselines.
card.limitation: Evaluations were limited to controlled phantom environments and a small set of subtasks, lacking diverse anatomies and longer procedures.

slides.title: C2Dex: Contact-Consistent Reconstruction and Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Monocular Video
slides.highlight: C2Dex improves the transfer of human manipulation behaviors from monocular video to dexterous robots by using stable object-side contacts to ensure physical plausibility and geometric consistency.

card.one_liner: C2Dex converts monocular human videos into executable dexterous robot trajectories using stable object-side contact representations.
card.key_idea: Aggregates frame-wise contacts in canonical object space to guide HOI reconstruction and uses Laplacian interaction optimization with residual RL for cross-embodiment retargeting.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on DexYCB and TACO; achieved success rates of 57.78% and 26.67% respectively, outperforming baselines. Validated via real-robot replay on Unitree G1.
card.limitation: Struggles with severe occlusions, extreme viewpoints, pose drift in object estimation, and complex in-hand manipulation like finger gaiting.

slides.title: World-to-Wrist: Task-Conditioned Future Wrist Modeling for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation
slides.tldr: FUTURE WRIST MODELING FOR FINE-GRAINED MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: W2-VLA improves fine-grained robot manipulation by forecasting future wrist latents conditioned on global task context and wrist history.

card.one_liner: W2W-VLA improves fine-grained robot manipulation by predicting future wrist-local latents conditioned on global task context.
card.key_idea: A VLM creates a latent interface shaped by structured CoT annotations; this interface and wrist history condition a predictor to forecast future wrist latents for action generation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on LIBERO (98.5% avg success), RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world tasks. Outperformed baselines like VLA-JEPA and π0, maintaining real-time generation above 80 Hz.
card.limitation: Full task completion remains difficult for highly contact-sensitive tasks, such as final alignment and insertion in bimanual plug insertion.
